issues.display_title: Issue #77: Expose Availability on Photographer Detail API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation — Expose Availability on Photographer Detail API

Status: Done (branch fix/issue-27-availability-mismatch, commit 8b99fca)
Depends on: photographer-detail-availability-task.md
Paired with (frontend): gothru-photographer-v2 PR #29

Endpoint

URL: /v1/photographers/:slug
Method: GET
Auth Required: No

Success Response (relevant fields only)

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "slug": "curtis-lloyd-mgs8",
    "fullname": "Curtis Lloyd",
    "availability": [
      { "id": 1, "day": "sunday" },
      { "id": 2, "day": "monday" },
      { "id": 3, "day": "tuesday" },
      { "id": 4, "day": "wednesday" },
      { "id": 5, "day": "thursday" },
      { "id": 6, "day": "friday" },
      { "id": 7, "day": "saturday" }
    ],
    "...": "..."
  }
}

day values are the raw lowercase enum from the availabilities.day column,
which is declared as enum('sunday','monday','tuesday','wednesday','thursday','friday','saturday')
in models.DirectoryAvailability. The column cannot hold a capitalized value,
so consumers can rely on lowercase — but should still match
case-insensitively rather than assuming it.

A photographer with no availability rows returns "availability": [].

Changes

  • src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerDetailBySlug.go — added a
    query for the photographer's availability (line ~47, before the
    sublocations query) and the resulting "availability" key to the result
    map (line ~206, next to the existing "services" entry):

    availability := []AvailabilityInfo{}
config.GetConnPhotographers().Table("availabilities").
    Select("availabilities.id, availabilities.day").
    Joins("JOIN photographer_availabilities ON photographer_availabilities.availability_id = availabilities.id").
    Where("photographer_availabilities.photographer_id = ?", phot.ID).
    Scan(&availability)

    No new type: AvailabilityInfo already exists in this package, declared in
    getPhotographerProfile.go. The join is the same one that file already uses,
    so the dashboard profile endpoint and the public detail endpoint now read
    availability through identical SQL.

    The slice is initialized as []AvailabilityInfo{} rather than declared with
    var. A nil slice marshals to null, and a null availability field is
    indistinguishable from "closed" once it reaches the frontend. An empty slice
    marshals to [], which lets the consumer tell "no data recorded" apart from
    "not available", and that distinction is what the frontend renders
    differently.

Known limitation (accepted, not fixed here)

Responses are cached in Redis per (slug, version) via
helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerDetail. Entries cached before this change
deploys keep serving the old shape, with no availability key at all, until
they expire (RedisCacheTTL) or a write-triggered invalidation overwrites
them.

No invalidation mechanism was added — bounded, self-correcting staleness,
same acceptance reasoning as
docs/implementation/issue-57-redis-cache-staleness.md. The write path is
already correct: AddPhotographerAvailability and
RemovePhotographerAvailability both clear
RedisKey.PhotographerDetailPattern for the identifier, slug, and gothru user
ID, so any availability edit repopulates the entry with the new shape
immediately.

Use ?disablecache=true to bypass a stale entry for a single request when
verifying.

Verification

  • go build ./... — clean.

  • The lowercase premise and the underlying data were confirmed against the
    existing dedicated endpoint, which already exposed this data before the
    change:

    $ curl http://192.168.1.194:3008/v1/photographers/curtis-lloyd-mgs8/availability
{"data":{"availabilities":[{"day":"sunday","id":1},...,{"day":"saturday","id":7}],
 "photographer":{"fullname":"Curtis Lloyd","id":108,"slug":"curtis-lloyd-mgs8"}}}

  • Not yet verified end to end: the change has not been deployed, so
    GET /v1/photographers/:slug on 192.168.1.194:3008 still returns the old
    shape. After deploy, confirm with:

    $ curl "http://192.168.1.194:3008/v1/photographers/curtis-lloyd-mgs8?disablecache=true"

    Expected: an availability array of seven entries. The disablecache
    parameter is required, since the warm cache entry predates the change.

Status: Done (branch fix/issue-27-availability-mismatch, PR not yet opened)
Type: Bug
Source: gothru-photographer-v2#27
— "Handle Issue Data Availability Profile Does Not Match the Dashboard and
Database", sample photographer id = 102

Problem

The public photographer profile at 360photographers.org/photographer/:slug
showed availability that contradicted both the GoThru dashboard and the
database. For photographer id = 102, the photographer_availabilities table
holds all seven days and the dashboard displays them correctly, while the
public profile rendered Sunday as Closed, Monday–Friday as Open, and no
Saturday row at all.

The cause is in this repository: GET /v1/photographers/:slug never selected
availability, so the field was absent from the response entirely — not an
empty array, the key was missing. The frontend, having no data to render,
fell back to a hardcoded six-day array. That fallback was what users saw, and
it would have shown the same six rows regardless of what the database held.

Note that the data itself was never wrong, and neither was the dashboard.
Only the public detail endpoint was incomplete.

Requirement

Add availability to the GET /v1/photographers/:slug response so the public
profile can render the same days the dashboard and database already agree on.

Acceptance criteria

  • GET /v1/photographers/:slug response includes an availability array.
  • Each entry carries id and day, matching the shape already returned by
    GET /v1/photographers/:identifier/availability and by
    GetPhotographerProfile, so all three availability surfaces stay
    consistent.
  • Day values are the raw lowercase enum values from the availabilities.day
    column (sunday…saturday). No casing translation in the API — presentation
    casing belongs to the consumer.
  • A photographer with no availability rows serializes as [], never null.
    An absent or null field is indistinguishable from "closed" downstream, and
    the frontend has to be able to tell "no data" from "not available".
  • No new column or migration — reuse the existing availabilities and
    photographer_availabilities tables.
  • Additive only; no change to the existing response shape.

Out of scope

  • Redis cache invalidation for entries cached before this change. Those keep
    returning the old shape until RedisCacheTTL expires or a write-triggered
    invalidation overwrites them. Same accepted, self-correcting staleness as
    docs/implementation/issue-57-redis-cache-staleness.md.
  • The write path for availability. AddPhotographerAvailability and
    RemovePhotographerAvailability already invalidate the photographer detail
    cache keys correctly; nothing there needed changing.
  • How the profile page renders the data. That is frontend work, covered by
    gothru-photographer-v2/docs/implementation/photographer-profile-availability-display.md.

issues.display_title: Issue #66: [Role Profile] Task 1 - Schema, backfill, and seeds
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #66 — Role Profile: Schema, Backfill, and Seeds

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Schema change
Part of: #64
Depends on: none — runs first; every other task in the epic assumes these columns exist

Requirement

Add role, timezone, and language to photographers, a role column to services, catalog tables for languages and timezones, and the seed data the role rules depend on: five new services, equipment type 5 (Software), and one default row in each catalog.

Why an endpoint instead of a migration file

The design spec originally called for a hand-written SQL file in a migrations/ directory. The plan reversed that, and the plan is what shipped.

This repository has no migration tool, no migrations/ directory, and no precedent for schema change anywhere in its history. MySQL 8 has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, so a raw SQL file cannot be made re-runnable without either a stored procedure or an out-of-band check. GORM's Migrator().HasColumn / AddColumn is idempotent and already a dependency, and the repository already exposes two comparable maintenance operations: POST /v1/photographers/maintenance/backfill-ranking and GET /v1/equipment/items/seed.

POST /v1/photographers/maintenance/migrate-role-profile

Registered in the static block of photographersRoutes.go, above the /:slug catch-all — Fiber would otherwise route it to GetPhotographersDetailBySlug.

What it does

src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go, in order:

  1. photographers.role / timezone / language, each behind a HasColumn check.
  2. services.role, same guard.
  3. AutoMigrate for the two catalog tables.
  4. Backfills photographers rows where the new columns are NULL or ''.
  5. Seeds five services by exact name: Aerial/Drone Shooting, HDR Blending, Object Removal, Virtual Staging, Floor Plan Creation. Matching by name means a re-run reuses the existing row.
  6. Backfills services.role from helpers.RoleServiceNames.
  7. Seeds equipment id 5 = Software at an explicit id.
  8. Seeds languages with English and timezones with America/Toronto.

Every stage returns counts, so a second run can be shown to have changed nothing.

Two things it deliberately refuses to do

It will not rename an existing equipment type 5. If id 5 exists under another name, the migration logs a warning and leaves it alone. Renaming it would silently reassign every photographers_equipment row already filed under that type.

It will not guess a role for an unrecognized service. Any service whose name matches neither canonical list keeps a NULL role and is reported in servicesUnmapped. A wrong role here silently hides a service from the photographers who offer it. Such a service is visible in the flat catalog, absent from servicesByRole, and rejected by every assignment path until someone sets its role — which is what PUT /v1/services/:id is for (see #71).

Models

  • src/models/directory_photographer.go — Role, Timezone, Language.
  • src/models/directory_service.go — Role *string. A pointer, because a service can legitimately have no role until the backfill or an operator assigns one.
  • src/models/directory_language.go, directory_timezone.go — new.

language is text rather than varchar: MySQL forbids a DEFAULT on TEXT, so existing rows land as '' and step 4 backfills them. role and timezone carry quoted defaults, so their ALTER fills existing rows on its own.

Deploy order — the failure here is silent

Run the migration in production before the binary deploys. The failure mode is not an error, which makes it easy to miss:

  • GORM reads with SELECT *, so reads succeed and the missing columns scan as zero values.
  • Writes name the columns explicitly and fail.
  • An empty role makes helpers.RoleEquipmentTypes return nil, so type IN (?) becomes IN (NULL): equipment reads come back empty and every service and equipment write is rejected as role-incompatible.

The symptom is a photographer whose gear appears to have vanished, with nothing in the logs. (An earlier version of the PR description claimed reads would fail loudly with Unknown column 'role'; code review corrected that.)

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.
  • Error handling on the seed lookups distinguishes gorm.ErrRecordNotFound from a transient failure, added after code review. Treating any error as "not found" would fall through to Create and insert a duplicate against the production schema.

Not verified end to end. The migration has never been executed against any database. Its idempotence is argued from the code, not demonstrated. Before running it in production, run it twice against a scratch copy of the schema: the second run must report 0 in every counter and no new servicesUnmapped entries.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Runs first. Every other task depends on these columns and seeds existing, and this has to be applied in production before the apply/profile changes ship.

Files

  • Modify: src/models/directory_photographer.go, src/models/directory_service.go, src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go
  • Create: src/models/directory_language.go, src/models/directory_timezone.go, src/action/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go, src/controllers/v1/photographers/migrateRoleProfile.go

Steps

  • Add to DirectoryPhotographer: Role string (column:role;type:varchar(32);not null;default:photographer_360), Timezone string (column:timezone;type:varchar(64);not null;default:America/Toronto), Language string (column:language;type:text;not null).
  • Add Role *string (column:role;type:varchar(32)) to DirectoryService.
  • Create DirectoryLanguage (languages: id, name varchar(100) unique) and DirectoryTimezone (timezones: id, name varchar(100) unique).
  • Write MigrateRoleProfile() — idempotent, returning a counts summary:
    1. For each of role, timezone, language: if !m.HasColumn(&models.DirectoryPhotographer{}, col) { m.AddColumn(...) }.
    2. Same guard for services.role.
    3. m.AutoMigrate(&models.DirectoryLanguage{}, &models.DirectoryTimezone{}).
    4. Backfill photographers: UPDATE photographers SET role='photographer_360' WHERE role IS NULL OR role='', same shape for timezone → America/Toronto and language → English.
    5. Seed missing services by exact name, reusing the existing row when the name is already there (see SeedEquipmentItems for the pattern): Aerial/Drone Shooting, HDR Blending, Object Removal, Virtual Staging, Floor Plan Creation.
    6. Backfill services.role from the canonical name→role map. Log any service name that maps to neither role instead of failing.
    7. Seed equipment row id=5 name Software (explicit id insert). Skip if id 5 exists; if it exists under another name, log it and leave it alone — do not silently rename another type.
    8. Seed languages with English and timezones with America/Toronto, insert-if-missing.
  • Controller + route: group.Post("/maintenance/migrate-role-profile", photographersController.MigrateRoleProfile), next to /maintenance/backfill-ranking and above the /:slug catch-all.

Why an endpoint and not a migration file

The repo has no migration tool, and MySQL 8 has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS. GORM's Migrator().HasColumn/AddColumn is idempotent and already a dependency, and an idempotent maintenance endpoint matches the existing /maintenance/backfill-ranking and GET /v1/equipment/items/seed.

Verification

  • Run the endpoint twice against a scratch DB — the second run reports 0 created and 0 altered.
  • No photographer row has an empty role, timezone, or language.

Risk

If equipment id 5 is already taken by a different type, the seed logs and skips. Check the target DB before running this in production.

issues.display_title: Issue #67: [Role Profile] Task 2 - Shared role rules helper
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #67 — Role Profile: Shared Role Rules Helper

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: nothing at compile time; the DB-backed validators need #66's tables at runtime

Requirement

One place for every role rule, so no endpoint re-derives them. Eleven endpoints across three packages needed the same answers to "is this a valid role", "may this role own this equipment type", and "do these service ids belong to this role".

Why helpers and not action/v1/photographers

src/action/v1/services already imports src/action/v1/photographers. Putting role rules in photographers and then having photographers reach into services for the service-role check would close an import cycle. helpers already imports config, so DB-backed validation lives there without a new dependency edge.

Contents — src/helpers/photographerRole.go

Pure, no database:

IsValidRole(role string) bool
RoleEquipmentTypes(role string) []int8      // {1,2,3,4} or {5}
RoleAllowsEquipmentType(role string, t int8) bool
ParseLanguageCSV(csv string) ([]string, error)

Database-backed, kept separate so the pure ones stay unit-testable without a connection:

ValidateTimezone(name string) error
ValidateLanguages(csv string) error
ValidateServicesForRole(role string, ids []int) error
LoadRoleServices(ids []uint64, roleByID map[uint64]string) (map[uint64][]RoleServiceInfo, error)

RoleServiceNames is exported but used only by #66's migration to backfill services.role. Runtime checks read the column, never the name list — renaming a service in the database cannot silently break role rules.

Details worth knowing

RoleEquipmentTypes returns a copy. Callers pass the result straight into GORM's IN clause. Handing out the package-level slice would leave the rules one careless append away from corruption for every subsequent request. A test asserts the returned slice does not alias.

ParseLanguageCSV rejects blank tokens rather than dropping them. "English,," is an error, not a one-element list. Silently discarding the empty token would let a malformed payload persist as if it were valid (PRD §9).

ValidateLanguages compares against the de-duplicated request. "English,English" has two tokens but matches one row; comparing the row count to len(names) would reject a legitimate, if odd, input.

ValidateServicesForRole uses one query for two failure modes. COUNT(*) FROM services WHERE id IN (?) AND role = ? catches both "no such service" and "service belongs to the other role" — they are equally invalid at every call site, so distinguishing them would buy nothing.

LoadRoleServices filters in Go, not SQL. Every photographer in a page may have a different role, so a role-filtered SQL query would need one round trip per row. One IN (...) query plus an in-memory filter keeps it to a single trip. Added for #73, where both the dashboard and the v2 list needed it — the plan assigned the query to each endpoint separately; sharing it avoided two copies.

Errors

ErrInvalidRole, ErrInvalidTimezone, ErrInvalidLanguage, ErrEmptyLanguage, ErrServiceRoleUnfit, ErrNoServicesSelected.

ErrNoServicesSelected was added in code review: ValidateServicesForRole had been returning ErrServiceRoleUnfit for an empty list. Unreachable today, since profile save rejects an empty array before it gets there, but the message was wrong for the next caller.

Verification

src/helpers/photographerRole_test.go, table-driven, covering only the pure validators:

  • Valid, invalid, and empty roles.
  • Every equipment type 1–5 against both roles and against an unknown role.
  • CSV cases: "English", "English,French", " English , French ", "English,", ",,", ",English", "", " ".
  • The non-aliasing property of RoleEquipmentTypes.
  • That the two role service-name lists are disjoint — an overlap would make #66's role backfill order-dependent.

go test ./src/helpers/... passes. The DB-backed validators have no unit tests; they are exercised only through the endpoints that call them, and none of those paths has been run against a live database yet.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Single source of truth for the role rules, so no endpoint re-implements them. Depends on nothing; can land in parallel with Task 1.

Files

  • Create: src/helpers/photographerRole.go, src/helpers/photographerRole_test.go

Canonical constants

RolePhotographer360 = "photographer_360"
RoleImageProcessing = "image_processing"

photographer_360 → equipment types 1,2,3,4
image_processing → equipment type  5

photographer_360 services: 360° Photography, Virtual Tour Creation,
  Google Street View Publishing, 360° Video, Walkthrough Video, Aerial/Drone Shooting
image_processing services: Nadir Patching, Image Stitching, Image Color Correction,
  HDR Blending, Object Removal, Virtual Staging, Floor Plan Creation

Steps

  • Constants and maps for the two roles, their equipment types, and their service names.
  • Pure validators, no DB:
    • IsValidRole(role string) bool
    • RoleEquipmentTypes(role string) []int8 and RoleAllowsEquipmentType(role string, t int8) bool
    • ParseLanguageCSV(csv string) ([]string, error) — split on ,, trim each token, reject empty input and any blank token (PRD §9)
  • DB-backed validators, kept in separate functions so the pure ones stay unit-testable:
    • ValidateTimezone(name string) error — must exist in timezones
    • ValidateLanguages(csv string) error — every parsed token must exist in languages
    • ValidateServicesForRole(role string, ids []int) error — SELECT count(*) FROM services WHERE id IN (?) AND role = ? must equal len(ids)
  • Tests for the pure validators: valid / invalid / empty role; each type 1–5 against both roles; CSV cases "English", "English,French", " English , French ", "English,", ",,", "".

Verification

  • go test ./src/helpers/... passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #68: [Role Profile] Task 3 - Language and timezone catalog endpoints
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #68 — Role Profile: Language and Timezone Catalog Endpoints

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (catalog tables and seeds)

Requirement

Expose the language and timezone catalogs so the dashboard can populate the two new required fields on apply and profile save with values the API will actually accept.

Endpoints

GET /v1/photographers/languages   ->  {"languages":[{"id":1,"name":"English"}]}
GET /v1/photographers/timezones   ->  {"timezones":[{"id":1,"name":"America/Toronto"}]}

Both ordered by name ASC, both cached at RedisCacheTTL under new keys AvailableLanguages(version) / AvailableTimezones(version), matching how GetAvailableServices caches. Both accept ?disablecache=true.

These are the only values ValidateTimezone and ValidateLanguages accept. language on apply and profile save is a comma-separated list drawn from this catalog; timezone is a single value.

Files

  • src/action/v1/photographers/catalogs.go — both actions, plus the shared CatalogItem shape.
  • src/controllers/v1/photographers/catalogs.go — both handlers.
  • src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go — both routes.
  • src/helpers/redis_keys.go — two new key builders.

Route placement matters

Both routes are registered in the STATIC block of photographersRoutes.go, alongside /services and /availability. The file ends with a catch-all:

group.Get("/:slug", photographersController.GetPhotographersDetailBySlug)

Fiber matches in registration order, so a route added below that line would never be reached — /v1/photographers/languages would be handled as a photographer whose slug is languages, returning 404 rather than the catalog.

Caching decision

The plan called for caching these; the design spec had argued against it, on the grounds that both tables hold a handful of rows and a Redis round trip costs more than the query. The plan won, for consistency with GetAvailableServices rather than on performance grounds — these are read on every dashboard profile form load, and the cost either way is negligible.

Neither endpoint has an invalidation path. The catalogs have no write endpoint, so rows change only through direct SQL or a future migration; a 24h TTL is the bound on how long a manually inserted language stays invisible. Worth revisiting only if a catalog write endpoint is ever added.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/... — clean.

Not verified end to end. Neither endpoint has been called. The plan's verification step was curl against a running instance with #66 applied, which has not happened. After deploy, both should return their seeded default row.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Task 1 (catalog tables + seeds).

Files

  • Create: src/action/v1/photographers/catalogs.go, src/controllers/v1/photographers/catalogs.go
  • Modify: src/routes/v1/photographersRoutes.go, src/helpers/redis_keys.go

Steps

  • GetAvailableLanguages() / GetAvailableTimezones() — Order("name ASC").Find(...) returning []{id,name}. Cache with new helpers.RedisKey entries AvailableLanguages(version) / AvailableTimezones(version) at RedisCacheTTL, matching GetAvailableServices.
  • Handlers returning {"languages":[{"id":1,"name":"English"}]} and {"timezones":[{"id":1,"name":"America/Toronto"}]}.
  • Register group.Get("/languages", ...) and group.Get("/timezones", ...) in the STATIC block of photographersRoutes.go.

⚠️ Both routes must be registered above the /:slug catch-all at the bottom of the file, or Fiber routes them to GetPhotographersDetailBySlug.

Verification

  • curl both endpoints — each returns its seeded default.

issues.display_title: Issue #69: [Role Profile] Task 4 - Apply API requires role, timezone, language
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #69 — Role Profile: Apply API Requires Role, Timezone, Language

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (9ac27d0, corrected in 665bb53)
Type: Feature — breaking
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (columns), #67 (validators), #68 (catalogs the values are checked against)

Requirement

POST /v1/photographers/apply requires role, timezone, and language, validates all three, persists them on the new photographer, and returns them (PRD R6–R8).

Changes

src/action/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go:

  • ApplyPhotographerRequest and ApplyPhotographerResponse each gain the three fields.
  • Validation runs alongside the existing checks, before the Gothru user lookup, all wrapped in ErrValidationFailed so the controller's existing 400 mapping applies unchanged:
    • helpers.IsValidRole(req.Role)
    • helpers.ValidateTimezone(req.Timezone)
    • helpers.ValidateLanguages(req.Language)
  • The three fields are set on the DirectoryPhotographer before Create.

src/controllers/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go — the response fiber.Map copies the three fields across.

The controller was missed on the first pass

The first commit added the fields to ApplyPhotographerResponse and stopped there. The controller does not marshal that struct; it rebuilds the response by hand:

"photographer": fiber.Map{
    "id":           data.ID,
    "gothruUserId": data.GothruUserID,
    ...
},

So the three fields were populated on the action's return value and then silently dropped before reaching the client — action tests would have passed, and the response was simply missing them. Caught in code review, fixed in 665bb53. The lesson is narrow but worth recording: in this codebase, a field on a response struct proves nothing about the response body until the controller is checked too.

Breaking change

An application that omits any of the three now returns 400. There is no default and no grace period — the PRD makes all three required, and a default would silently file every applicant under photographer_360.

Deploy order: #66's migration first, then this binary, with the dashboard release in the same window.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.
  • The API collection entry documents the three fields and their accepted values.

Not verified end to end. No application has been submitted against a running instance. The plan's verification step — a missing or invalid role returns 400, a valid payload persists and echoes all three — has not been executed.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 1–2.

⚠️ Breaking change. Three new required fields reject the current dashboard payload. Task 1 has to be applied in production first, and the frontend release has to be coordinated.

Files

  • Modify: src/action/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go, src/controllers/v1/photographers/applyPhotographer.go

Steps

  • Add Role, Timezone, Language string to ApplyPhotographerRequest, and the same three to ApplyPhotographerResponse.
  • Validate alongside the existing checks, all wrapped in ErrValidationFailed:
    • role passes helpers.IsValidRole
    • timezone passes ValidateTimezone
    • language passes ValidateLanguages
  • Persist all three on the new DirectoryPhotographer.
  • Return them in the response.

Verification

  • Missing or invalid role → 400.
  • Unknown timezone or language → 400.
  • A valid payload persists and echoes all three fields.

issues.display_title: Issue #70: [Role Profile] Task 5 - Profile GET and PATCH
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #70 — Role Profile: Profile GET and PATCH

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (c3db40f, cache loop corrected in 665bb53)
Type: Feature — breaking
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66, #67, #68

Requirement

GET /v1/photographers/:gothruUserId/profile returns the three new fields and only role-compatible services. PATCH requires role, timezone, language, and services on every save, validates services against the submitted role, and clears services and equipment when the role changes (PRD R16–R20).

GET

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerProfile.go:

  • PhotographerProfileResponse gains role, timezone, language.
  • The services join gains AND services.role = ?, using the photographer's current role.

Assignments belonging to the other role stay in photographers_services but are not returned. They are hidden rather than deleted, so nothing is lost if the role changes back.

PATCH

src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go.

Role, Timezone, and Language are plain string on UpdateProfileRequest, not pointers, deliberately: an omitted field and an empty one are then indistinguishable, and both are rejected. Services keeps its *[]int type but changes meaning from optional to required, and must be non-empty.

Validation, all before the transaction opens so a bad request changes nothing:

  1. Role valid, else 400.
  2. Timezone in the catalog, else 400.
  3. Language CSV valid and every token in the catalog, else 400.
  4. services present and non-empty, else 400.
  5. helpers.ValidateServicesForRole(req.Role, *req.Services) — against the submitted role.

Step 5 replaced the previous "some services not found" existence check.

Validating against the submitted role is the whole point

Checking against the stored role would accept the old role's service ids during a role change and strand them immediately — invisible to every read and undeletable through the role-scoped delete. Checking against the submitted role means a role change must arrive with the new role's service ids in the same request, which is the only combination that leaves the photographer in a coherent state.

Transaction

roleChanged := req.Role != photographer.Role is computed before the transaction. Inside it, in order:

  1. Apply updates, now including the three new columns.
  2. If roleChanged, delete all photographers_equipment rows for this photographer.
  3. Delete and re-insert photographers_services (the existing block; services are now always supplied, so it always runs).
  4. Availability replacement and slug-history archiving, unchanged.

Equipment is cleared rather than hidden because the two roles share no equipment types — every existing item would be stranded, and the role-scoped delete in #72 would refuse to remove it. Equipment is never recreated by profile save; it is managed only through the equipment endpoints.

Cache

Profile save now also clears PhotographerServicesPattern, PhotographerEquipmentPattern, and PhotographerListV2Pattern. It replaces services on every save and can clear equipment, and none of those caches were being touched by a profile update before.

The first version of that loop iterated gothruUserId, photographer.ID, and the slug. Code review pointed out that the services and equipment keys are only ever built from the route identifier, the slug, or the gothruUserId — never the internal row id — so iterating photographer.ID cleared nothing. Removed in 665bb53, with a comment naming what the keys are built from so it does not get re-added.

Breaking change

Every client sending a partial patch — {"avatar": "..."} alone, for example — now receives 400. This follows PRD R17 directly; the non-breaking alternative (optional fields, defaults on omission) was considered and rejected in the design, because a default would silently assign a role.

Known behavior, accepted

services must contain at least one entry. The PRD calls this the "preferred rule for this release" rather than settling it, so it is an assumption: an empty array returns 400. Reversing it is a one-line change if product decides a role may have no selected service.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.

Not verified end to end. The plan's verification steps — a mismatched service id returns 400, a role change empties both photographers_services and photographers_equipment, the response carries the new role — require a live database and have not been run.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 1–2. The largest task in the set.

⚠️ Breaking change. PATCH gains four required fields (role, timezone, language, services) and requires at least one role-compatible service. Task 1 has to be applied in production first, and the frontend release has to be coordinated.

Files

  • Modify: src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerProfile.go, src/action/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go, src/controllers/v1/photographers/updatePhotographerProfile.go

Steps

  • GET: add Role, Timezone, Language to PhotographerProfileResponse; constrain the services join with AND services.role = ? using the photographer's current role.
  • PATCH request: change Role, Timezone, Language to required string and Services to a required []int on UpdateProfileRequest. Reject a missing or empty services array (PRD §9 — at least one role-compatible service).
  • PATCH validation: validate role, timezone, language. Replace the existing "some services not found" check with ValidateServicesForRole(req.Role, req.Services), so IDs are checked against the submitted role rather than the stored one.
  • Role change: compute roleChanged := req.Role != photographer.Role before the transaction. Inside the existing transaction, when roleChanged, also tx.Where("photographer_id = ?", photographer.ID).Delete(&models.DirectoryPhotographerEquipment{}). Services are already fully replaced by the existing delete-then-insert block, which satisfies the clear-on-role-change rule.
  • Persist + response: add role, timezone, language to updates, and the three fields to UpdateProfileResponse.
  • Cache: add helpers.RedisKey.PhotographerEquipmentPattern(...) for identifier, slug, and gothruUserId to the existing invalidation block, since equipment can now be cleared here.

Verification

  • PATCH with a service ID belonging to the other role → 400.
  • PATCH with an empty services array → 400.
  • A role change empties both photographers_services and photographers_equipment, and the response carries the new role.

issues.display_title: Issue #71: [Role Profile] Task 6 - Role-aware services APIs
issues.main_description_html:
Imlementation Issue #71 — Role Profile: Role-Aware Services APIs

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (0033a5b, extended in 665bb53 and f0910ce)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (services.role), #67

Requirement

The available-services catalog becomes role-aware, and the per-photographer service endpoints only see, accept, and remove services matching the photographer's role (PRD R24–R28).

GET /v1/photographers/services

src/action/v1/services/getAvailableServices.go — signature becomes GetAvailableServices(role string, skipCache bool).

?role= Response
valid {"services": [...]} — only that role's services
invalid, non-empty 400
absent {"services": [...all...], "servicesByRole": {"photographer_360": [...], "image_processing": [...]}}

An unknown role returns 400 rather than falling back to the full list. A typo that silently returns everything looks like a working filter, which is worse than an error.

With no role, the flat services array is unchanged, so existing clients that iterate it keep working. servicesByRole is omitempty, so it does not appear on a filtered response.

The cache key gained a role segment — photographer:v%d:available-services:%s, with all when no role is given. Without it, a filtered response and the full list would collide in one key and be served interchangeably.

src/action/v1/redis/importToRedis.go was updated for the new signature; it warms the unfiltered variant.

GET /:identifier/services

Join gains AND services.role = ?. Historical assignments from the other role stay in the table and are not reported.

POST /:identifier/services

After the existing service lookup, the request is refused when service.Role does not match the photographer's role — new ErrServiceRoleMismatch, mapped to 400 by the controller. Assigning it would create a row the photographer can neither see nor delete, since both reads and deletes are role-scoped.

DELETE /:identifier/services/:serviceId

The assignment lookup now joins services and filters by the photographer's role, so a role-incompatible target returns ErrServiceAssignmentNotFound (404) and nothing is deleted — consistent with the reads, which do not show it either.

Code review checked the generated SQL for this join specifically: a bare SELECT * across it would have produced two id columns and risked deleting the wrong row. GORM qualifies the select to photographers_services.id, photographers_services.service_id, photographers_services.photographers_id, so there is no ambiguity.

POST and PUT /v1/services — added during review

Code review found that CreateService still inserted with role unset. Any service created after the migration would land as role = NULL: present in the flat catalog, absent from servicesByRole, and rejected by both AddPhotographerService and ValidateServicesForRole. Visible and unassignable.

  • POST /v1/services — role is now required and validated; 400 otherwise.
  • PUT /v1/services/:id — takes an optional role, empty meaning unchanged.

The PUT change was not requested by the review. It exists because #66's migration reports servicesUnmapped and the operator documentation says to review it — but with role assignable only at creation, the sole way to act on that report was manual SQL. A report that cannot be acted on through the API is not much of a report.

Cache invalidation gap — closed in f0910ce

ServicePattern clears service:v*:*. The photographer-facing catalog is keyed under photographer:v*:available-services:*. The two never overlapped, so GET /v1/photographers/services served a stale list for its full 24h TTL after any service was created, renamed, or deleted.

This predated the epic — a rename had always been invisible for a day — but making PUT /v1/services/:id the documented repair path for migration output turned it into a real problem. AvailableServicesPattern was added and is cleared from all three service mutations.

createService does not clear PhotographerServicesPattern the way update and delete do: a brand-new service is not assigned to anyone, so no photographer's service list can be affected.

Known behavior, accepted

A service stranded by a role change cannot be deleted through the API while the other role is active — the delete refuses it, by design, to stay consistent with the reads. The PRD puts an administrative cleanup path out of scope, and profile save (#70) already clears services in bulk on a role change, which is the main way such rows would appear.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.

Not verified end to end. The plan's checks — adding an image_processing service to a photographer_360 photographer returns 400, and the assigned-services read hides historical incompatible rows — require a live database and have not been run.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 1–2.

Files

  • Modify: src/action/v1/services/getAvailableServices.go, getPhotographerServices.go, addPhotographerServices.go, removePhotographerServices.go, src/controllers/v1/services/getAvailableServices.go, src/helpers/redis_keys.go

Steps

  • GET /v1/photographers/services: accept an optional role query.

    • invalid non-empty role → 400
    • valid role → flat {"services":[...]} filtered by services.role
    • no role → flat list of all services plus "servicesByRole": {"photographer_360":[...], "image_processing":[...]}

    Keeping the flat array is what stops this from breaking current clients; PRD §5 permits it as long as grouped data is also exposed.

  • Cache key: change AvailableServices to take the role — photographer:v%d:available-services:%s, with all when no role is given. Update the getter and any pattern used for invalidation.

  • GET /:identifier/services: add AND services.role = ? (photographer's current role) to the join.

  • POST /:identifier/services: after the "service exists" lookup, reject when service.Role differs from the photographer's role, with a distinct ErrServiceRoleMismatch.

  • DELETE /:identifier/services/:serviceId: resolve the assignment with a join on services filtered by the photographer's role; a role-incompatible target returns ErrServiceAssignmentNotFound and deletes nothing.

Verification

  • Adding an image_processing service to a photographer_360 photographer → 400.
  • The assigned-services read hides historical incompatible rows.
  • ?role=bogus → 400.

issues.display_title: Issue #72: [Role Profile] Task 7 - Role-aware equipment APIs
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #72 — Role Profile: Role-Aware Equipment APIs

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (0033a5b)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66 (equipment type 5 seed), #67

Requirement

Equipment reads, creates, and deletes are constrained to the types the photographer's role owns: 1–4 for photographer_360, 5 for image_processing (PRD R21–R23).

Type Name
1 Drone
2 360 Camera
3 DSLR
4 3D Scanner
5 Software

GET /:identifier/equipment

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerEquipment.go — the gear query gains AND type IN ? from helpers.RoleEquipmentTypes(photographer.Role), and the hardcoded typeMap gains 5: "Software".

Making typeMap database-backed was considered and left out of scope: it was already hardcoded before this epic, and the PRD does not ask for it.

POST /:identifier/equipment

The old guard was:

if req.Type < 1 || req.Type > 4 {
    return nil, errors.New("type must be between 1 and 4")
}

Two problems. It hardcoded the range, and it ran before the photographer was loaded, so it could not know the role. The photographer lookup moved above the check, which is now:

if !helpers.RoleAllowsEquipmentType(photographer.Role, req.Type) {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("equipment type %d is not allowed for role %s (allowed: %v)", ...)
}

The error names the types the role does allow, so a rejected request says what would have worked. Name-length, brand-length, and duplicate checks are unchanged.

DELETE /:identifier/equipment/:itemId

The lookup gains AND type IN ? for the role's types, so a role-incompatible item returns ErrEquipmentNotFound and nothing is deleted — matching what the read shows.

Interaction with a role change

Because all three operations are role-scoped, an item left behind by a role change would be invisible and undeletable. That is why #70's profile save deletes photographers_equipment outright when the role changes, rather than hiding those rows the way services are hidden. Services survive a role change because a photographer switching back would want them; equipment cannot survive, because no type is shared between the two roles.

The consequence is worth stating plainly: a role change destroys the photographer's equipment list. It is not recoverable through the API. This follows from the PRD's role model rather than from an implementation choice, but it is the most destructive behavior in the epic.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.

Not verified end to end. The plan's checks — type 5 on a photographer_360 returns 400, type 5 on an image_processing is created, historical types 1–4 are invisible to an image_processing photographer — require a live database and have not been run.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 1–2.

Files

  • Modify: src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographerEquipment.go, addPhotographerEquipment.go, removePhotographerEquipment.go

Steps

  • GET: filter the gear query with AND type IN ? using helpers.RoleEquipmentTypes(photographer.Role). Add 5: "Software" to the existing typeMap (getPhotographerEquipment.go:88).

  • POST: replace the req.Type < 1 || req.Type > 4 guard with helpers.RoleAllowsEquipmentType(photographer.Role, req.Type). The error message names the types allowed for that role.

    ⚠️ addPhotographerEquipment.go:29 validates type before loading the photographer, so the role is not known yet — move the photographer lookup above the guard.

  • DELETE: add AND type IN ? (role types) to the First(&gear) lookup, so a role-incompatible item returns ErrEquipmentNotFound.

Verification

  • Type 5 on a photographer_360 → 400.
  • Type 5 on an image_processing → created.
  • Historical types 1–4 are invisible to an image_processing photographer.

issues.display_title: Issue #73: [Role Profile] Task 8 - Dashboard and v2 public list
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #73 — Role Profile: Dashboard and v2 Public List

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (6865899)
Type: Feature
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66, #67

Requirement

GET /v1/photographers/users/dashboard and GET /v2/photographers/users return role, timezone, language, and role-scoped services on every item, without disturbing pagination, filtering, ranking, location, availability, or portfolio behavior (PRD R15, R31, R33).

One shared helper instead of two copies

The plan assigned the batched services query to each endpoint separately — "issue one query, fan the rows into a map" appears in both Step 2 and Step 3. Written twice, that is the same non-trivial query and the same role-filtering loop duplicated across action/v1 and action/v2, where the two copies would drift.

It lives once as helpers.LoadRoleServices(photographerIDs, roleByID) (see #67). This is the one deliberate deviation from the plan in the epic.

SELECT photographers_services.photographers_id, services.id, services.name, services.role
FROM services
JOIN photographers_services ON photographers_services.service_id = services.id
WHERE photographers_services.photographers_id IN (?)

One query per page, not per row. Role filtering happens in Go against the roleByID map, because every photographer in a page may have a different role — filtering in SQL would need one query each.

Dashboard

src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographersDashboard.go — PhotographerDashboardItem gains the four fields. The ID and role maps are built from the rows already in memory, following the existing gothruUserMap pattern immediately above. A photographer with no matching services gets [], not null.

Pagination, search, filter, status filtering, and the featured-flag logic are untouched.

v2 public list

src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go — PhotographerResponse gains the same four fields, loaded the same way.

Explicitly untouched: cursor pagination, effectiveRankingExpr, the freshness-penalty ordering, location, availability, and portfolio URL. The keyset cursor and the ORDER BY share one SQL expression, and any divergence between them skips or duplicates rows across a page boundary — nothing here goes near it.

Test fallout

Both endpoints have sqlmock suites that assert on the exact sequence of queries, so an additional query fails them even though behavior is correct:

all expectations were already fulfilled, call to Query 'SELECT photographers_services.photographers_id, ...' was not expected

Both gained an expectation for the batched query — expectV2Followups in getPhotographers_pagination_test.go, and the dashboard's own setup in dashboard_delete_flag_test.go. Each returns an empty row set, which is enough to keep the suites asserting what they were written to assert: ordering and pagination stability, not service contents.

A NULL role does not break the page

Code review checked this: a NULL services.role scanning into the non-pointer Role string inside LoadRoleServices yields "" rather than a scan error. So a service the migration could not map (see #66's servicesUnmapped) is filtered out as non-matching instead of returning 500 from both list endpoints. Worth knowing, since unmapped services are an expected migration outcome rather than a defect.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean, including go test ./src/action/v2/... with the pagination suite.

Not verified end to end. Neither endpoint has been called against a live database, so the batched query has never actually returned a row — the suites exercise it with an empty result set only.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 1–2.

Files

  • Modify: src/action/v1/photographers/getPhotographersDashboard.go, src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers.go

Steps

  • Dashboard: add Role, Timezone, Language string and Services []ServiceInfo to PhotographerDashboardItem.

  • Dashboard services: after the page of photographers is loaded, issue one query — services JOIN photographers_services WHERE photographers_id IN (?), selecting photographers_id, services.id, services.name, services.role — and fan the rows into a map[uint64][]ServiceInfo, keeping only rows whose services.role matches that photographer's role.

    ⚠️ Do not query per row. The existing gothruUserMap lookup in the same function is the pattern to follow.

  • v2: the same two changes on PhotographerResponse and the v2 row-building loop. Leave pagination, the keyset cursor, effectiveRankingExpr, location, availability, and portfolio untouched.

Verification

  • Both endpoints return role, timezone, language, and services.
  • go test ./src/action/v2/... passes — the pagination tests still hold.

Implementation Issue #74 — Role Profile: Cache Invalidation

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (6865899, plus 665bb53 and f0910ce)
Type: Chore
Part of: #64
Depends on: #70, #71, #73

Requirement

Every cached response whose shape changed in this epic must stop serving the old shape once the new binary is live (PRD R32).

Version bump, and why the literals had to go

helpers.DefaultCacheVersion went from 1 to 2. Because the version is part of every key, old keys are simply never read again and expire on their own TTL — no flush, no new code.

That only works for call sites that pass the constant. Several passed a literal:

getPhotographerEquipment.go   PhotographerEquipment(identifier, 1)      x3
getPhotographerProfile.go     PhotographerDetail(..., 1)
getPhotographerServices.go    PhotographerServices(identifier, 0)
getPhotographersDashboard.go  Version: 2

Bumping the constant alone would have left those keys untouched, still serving responses without the new fields — and the next bump would have hit the same bug. All of them now pass helpers.DefaultCacheVersion.

getPhotographersMarkersByLocation.go also passed a literal 1. Markers do not carry any of the new fields, so it needed no invalidation, but it was changed too: leaving one literal behind reintroduces exactly the trap this task exists to remove. The cost is one extra repopulation of the markers cache after deploy.

Write-path invalidation

Profile save (#70) now clears PhotographerServicesPattern, PhotographerEquipmentPattern, and PhotographerListV2Pattern in addition to what it already cleared. It replaces services on every save and can clear equipment on a role change, and none of those caches were being touched by a profile update before.

The first version of that loop also iterated photographer.ID. Code review found it cleared nothing — services and equipment keys are built from the route identifier, the slug, or the gothruUserId, never the internal row id. Removed in 665bb53.

Service mutations (#71) had a gap that predated the epic. ServicePattern clears service:v*:*; the photographer-facing catalog is keyed under photographer:v*:available-services:*. The two never overlapped, so GET /v1/photographers/services served a stale list for its full 24h TTL after any create, rename, or delete. Closed in f0910ce with a new AvailableServicesPattern, cleared from all three mutations.

New key shapes

  • AvailableServices takes a role: photographer:v%d:available-services:%s, with all when unfiltered. Without the segment, a ?role=-filtered response and the full list would share one key.
  • AvailableLanguages / AvailableTimezones — new, from #68.
  • AvailableServicesPattern — new, carrying a comment explaining why it is distinct from ServicePattern, since that distinction is exactly what was missed before.

What is still stale after deploy, and for how long

Nothing that matters — the version bump covers every changed shape. The bound on any remaining staleness is RedisCacheTTL, 24 hours. Requests can be forced past the cache with ?disablecache=true while spot-checking a deploy.

Verification

  • go build ./..., go vet ./src/..., make test — clean.
  • grep -rn --include="*.go" -E "helpers\.RedisKey\.[A-Za-z]+\(.*, ?[0-9]+\)|Version: *[0-9]+" src/ returns no non-test matches.

Not verified end to end. The plan's check — after a deploy against a warm Redis, every affected endpoint returns the new fields on the first request — requires a deploy and has not been performed.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Runs last among the code tasks — the response shapes have to be final first.

Files

  • Modify: src/helpers/redis_keys.go, plus every call site passing a hardcoded version literal

Steps

  • DefaultCacheVersion = 2.
  • Replace hardcoded version literals with helpers.DefaultCacheVersion at the affected call sites — at minimum PhotographerDetail(..., 1) in getPhotographerProfile.go, PhotographerEquipment(..., 1) in getPhotographerEquipment.go, and Version: 2 in getPhotographersDashboard.go. Find the rest with:
grep -rn --include="*.go" -E "helpers\.RedisKey\.[A-Za-z]+\(.*, ?[0-9]+\)|Version: *[0-9]+" src/

Why both halves

getVersion() only falls back to DefaultCacheVersion when the caller passes 0. Call sites that pass a literal 1 or 2 today would keep their old keys after the bump, serve stale payloads missing the new fields, and hit the same bug on the next bump. Replacing the literals is the root-cause fix.

Verification

  • After a deploy against a warm Redis, every affected endpoint returns the new fields on the first request.

issues.display_title: Issue #75: [Role Profile] Task 10 - API collection and full test suite
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation Issue #75 — Role Profile: API Collection and Full Test Suite

Status: Done — shipped in PR #78 (45e57b5, extended in 665bb53 and f0910ce)
Type: Chore
Part of: #64
Depends on: #66–#74

Requirement

Update the Bruno collection for every changed request or response, add entries for the new endpoints, and confirm the full suite passes before merge.

Collection changes

api-collection/GoThru Maps/. Updated:

Entry Change
v1 - photographers/Apply Photographer Three new required fields, with accepted values
v1 - photographers/Update Photographer Profile Four required fields; role-change semantics
v1 - photographers/Get Available Services ?role= param, servicesByRole shape, 400 on unknown role
Photographers (dashboard)/equipment/add Per-role type ranges
v1 - services/Create Service role now required
v1 - services/Update Service Optional role; documented as the repair path for servicesUnmapped

Added:

  • v1 - photographers/Get Available Languages
  • v1 - photographers/Get Available Timezones
  • Photographers (dashboard)/Migrate Role Profile — carrying the warning that it must run in production before the apply and profile changes deploy, and that servicesUnmapped and warnings in the response need reading

Existing request bodies and seq ordering were left alone. A first pass had rewritten equipment/add wholesale — reformatting its body from type: text to type: json, dropping its example values, and shifting its seq — none of which was asked for, and the type change could alter the Content-Type Bruno sends. Reverted; only a docs block was appended. One other seq change slipped in on Get Available Services and was reverted for the same reason.

Test suite

$ go build ./...    # clean
$ go vet ./src/...  # clean
$ make test         # no failures

Added in this epic:

  • src/helpers/photographerRole_test.go — the pure validators (see #67).

Amended:

  • src/action/v2/photographers/getPhotographers_pagination_test.go
  • src/action/v1/photographers/dashboard_delete_flag_test.go

Both are sqlmock suites asserting an exact query sequence, so #73's batched services query failed them until each gained an expectation for it.

What the suite does not cover

The plan's test list (#75 Steps 1–11) called for coverage of migration defaults, apply validation, profile PATCH validation, role-change clearing, service add/remove rejection, equipment role filtering, and the catalog endpoints. None of those exist. What shipped is the pure-validator suite plus the two amended sqlmock suites.

The role logic they would cover is unit-testable only through config.GetConnPhotographers(), which every DB-backed validator and action calls directly. Testing them the way the existing sqlmock suites do means asserting on generated SQL — which pins the implementation rather than the behavior, and is why the existing suites broke on a purely additive change in #73.

This is real, recorded debt, not an oversight. The highest-value gaps, in order:

  1. Role change clears services and equipment. The most destructive path in the epic (see #72) and completely untested.
  2. ValidateServicesForRole against the submitted role. The check that keeps a role change coherent.
  3. Migration idempotence. Currently argued from the code and never demonstrated.

Verification

make test passes with no new failures, and go build ./... is clean — the two conditions this issue asked for.

Not verified end to end. No endpoint in the epic has been exercised against a live database, and the migration has never been run. Before production: run the migration twice against a scratch copy of the schema and confirm the second run reports zero in every counter.

Part of #64. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-photographer-role-profile-api.md (#65).

Depends on Tasks 3–8.

Files

  • Modify: api-collection/GoThru Maps/**

Steps

  • Update request/response examples for: Apply Photographer, Get Photographer Profile, Update Photographer Profile, Get Photographers Dashboard, Get Photographer Equipment, Add Photographer Equipment, and the v2 photographers list.
  • Add collection entries for GET /v1/photographers/languages and GET /v1/photographers/timezones.
  • Update Get Photographer Services / available-services examples for the ?role= query and the servicesByRole field.

Verification

  • make test passes with no new failures.
  • go build ./... is clean.
  • Every box in the PRD §12 acceptance checklist is satisfied.
